questions.question: Where does the String pool live in Java 7 and later?
questions.explanation: Java 7 moved the pool out of the fixed-size PermGen into the heap, so unused pooled strings can be garbage collected.

questions.question: What does this print? String a = "Dock"; String b = new String("Dock"); System.out.println(a == b);
questions.explanation: new always creates a separate heap object, so the two references point to different objects even though the text matches.

questions.question: What does this print? String a = "BusStop"; String b = "Bus" + "Stop"; System.out.println(a == b);
questions.explanation: Both operands are literals, so javac joins them into the constant "BusStop", which is the same pooled object as a.

questions.question: What does this print? String x = "Bus"; String b = x + "Stop"; System.out.println(b == "BusStop");
questions.explanation: x is not a constant variable, so the join happens at run time and creates a new object outside the pool.

questions.question: When is final String P = ...; P + "-9" joined by the compiler?
options: Only when P is set to a constant expression such as a literal
Never; + always runs at run time
questions.explanation: A final variable is a compile-time constant only when its initializer is a constant expression. A value from a method call is not.

questions.question: What does s.intern() return when the pool already holds a string equal to s?
options: The object already stored in the pool
questions.explanation: intern() returns the pooled object for that text. Only when the text is new does it add s and return s.

questions.question: At most how many String objects does new String("Quay") create if "Quay" was never used before?
questions.explanation: The literal "Quay" is added to the pool, and new creates a second object on the heap.

questions.question: A check if (input == "yes") works in a unit test with a literal but fails when input comes from Scanner. Why?
options: Text read at run time is a new object, so == compares different addresses
Scanner adds hidden spaces to every word
questions.explanation: Input creates new String objects outside the pool. Use "yes".equals(input) to compare the characters.

questions.question: A program stores 1 million status labels with new String("READY") and uses far more memory than expected. What is the fix?
options: Use the literal "READY" so every label shares one pooled object
questions.explanation: new String creates one object per call. Assigning the literal gives every element the same pooled object.

questions.question: Why is it safe for many variables to share one pooled String object?
options: The pool is locked with synchronized
Each variable gets a private copy on first write
Pooled strings are stored on the stack
String is immutable, so no holder can change the shared text
questions.explanation: No method can modify a String, so a change made through one reference can never surprise another reference.
